identity.name: LangGraph
identity.one_liner: Framework for building long-running, stateful agents with controllable workflows.
identity.short_description: LangGraph is an open-source framework for building stateful, durable agent workflows where developers need explicit control over graphs, state, checkpoints, and human-in-the-loop behavior.

positioning.why_it_matters: LangGraph matters because many serious agents are not simple prompt chains. They need state, branching, recovery, and clear control over what happens between model calls and tool calls.
best_for: Teams that need controllable workflows, checkpoints, and human review
Builders already using LangChain or nearby model/tool abstractions
not_for: Users who want a fully managed consumer product with no setup work
Teams that cannot review the linked source, license, and operational requirements before adoption

core_strengths.title: Stateful graph architecture
core_strengths.description: LangGraph models agent flows as graphs with explicit state transitions.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: This gives developers more control than a hidden loop inside a generic agent runner.

core_strengths.title: Durable and interruptible workflows
core_strengths.description: Its design supports checkpointing, human review, and continuation.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Long-running agents need to pause, resume, and recover safely.

core_strengths.title: Large ecosystem fit
core_strengths.description: LangGraph connects into the LangChain ecosystem and common model/tool integrations.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: A framework is easier to adopt when surrounding integrations already exist.
